output.title: The quiet cost of model deprecation
output.body:
If you are weighing automation against another hire, do not only compare the first build. Compare what happens when the model underneath the workflow is upgraded, retired, or repriced. That is the quiet cost: the work may still exist, but the upkeep can change.

For a small business, the issue shows up in ordinary workflows like customer inquiry triage, lead qualification, or invoice handling. A simple flow can look fine at launch and still need attention later if the underlying model changes. That is not a disaster. It is a planning item.

The practical next step is to ask one blunt question before you approve the pilot: if the model changes, does this workflow keep working, or do we need to rebuild parts of it and decide again whether it still beats manual work? If that answer is vague, the plan is not complete yet.

If you want the comparison to be honest, define who owns the model-version decision and who approves any re-investment before money moves. Otherwise the cheapest entry price can hide the future maintenance bill. That is where the hidden cost stops being quiet.
